citations.review_text:
For whatever reason, it completely crashes the GPU after switching to 1440p. I did some research and came to the conclusion that the game's engine somehow struggles to play at 1440p with a modern GPU. The engine crashes the GPU to the point where you have to use the game's launcher to set it all up manually all over again (or verify the files). However, even at lower resolutions, the game simply is not worth the struggle. The only way to make it playable is in windowed mode, but after 10  minutes of gameplay, it still crashes.
Somehow the frametime reaches 500ms after 5 minutes into the game. 
I'm running  9070 XT by the way.
Refuses to show keyboard prompts or allow remapping unless I disable steam input. Graphics options and keybind changes refuse to save between launches. Refund time!

I went into Mafia: Definitive Edition completely blind, and I honestly didn't expect it to be this good. I won't include any spoilers because this is absolutely a game that's best experienced for yourself.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe vehicle handling and driving mechanics as clunky or difficult to control.

citations.review_text:
This is [b]one of the[/b] worst games I have ever played where I had to tolerate its issues.

I know you'll defend the game, saying it's good. I won't argue with you; it really is. It has a good story and good music, not to mention the clunky car controls. Plus, there's a Free Play (Free Ride) for exploring Lost Heaven, particularly for gathering collectibles.

But I still can't give it a good rating because of these constant freezing and crashing issues. That's why I don't want to waste my time on the Classic difficulty, which will probably be a double nightmare.

Mafia: Definitive Edition is a mixed bag — gorgeous in some ways, rough in others, but still worth the ride.

The good:
The story is genuinely great. It pulls you into the era and nails that retro gangster vibe. The visual fidelity on faces and cars is impressive — you can actually see pores on characters' faces. The music, sound design, models, and textures all show real craftsmanship. Kudos to the team for that.

The bad:
Controls and animations feel clunky and dated. Vehicle handling is particularly rough — maybe that's intentional, to reflect how much harder cars were to drive back then, but it still doesn't feel great to play.

There are also technical issues: I get latency/stutter in fullscreen mode that disappears in borderless windowed, but borderless windowed itself bugs out on relaunch and defaults back to fullscreen — I have to keep toggling between the two a few times until it randomly fixes itself. The forced anti-aliasing leaves noticeable ghosting/trails, and the lack of DLAA support is disappointing.

New York itself feels pale and lifeless — streets feel like an empty sandbox with just a handful of NPCs and cars scattered around. Combined with the technical issues, it gives the impression this was more of a straight port to a new engine than a full remake, so the world ends up feeling plasticky and under-detailed. Half-finished, almost.

Verdict:
Despite all these issues, I'd still recommend it. It's a unique chance to relive the life of a gangster in that era, and the story and atmosphere carry it even when the tech doesn't.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that gunplay and combat mechanics feel stiff or imprecise.

citations.review_text:
Being familiar with the original, I think Mafia: Definitive Edition does a great job modernising the classic while preserving what made the story so memorable.

Unfortunately, the gameplay is much less impressive. I don't mind the story and missions following a linear structure, but the gunplay felt imprecise, with combat relying too heavily on sticking to cover.

I enjoyed my time with it, but once the story was over, I had little motivation to return. Even collecting the remaining collectibles felt more confusing than rewarding. Overall, it's a good remake with a great story, but playing it once will suffice.
Gameplay is a little stiff but very good per total, the story was amazing, felt like a movie.

claims.claim: Reviewers praise the game's story, cutscenes, and 1930s atmosphere.

citations.review_text:
Mafia: Definitive Edition is probably one of the best examples of how to remake an old game properly.

The original Mafia came out in 2002, and instead of just making it look a bit prettier and calling it a day, Hangar 13 basically rebuilt the whole thing.

And honestly, it works really well.

You play as Tommy Angelo, a taxi driver in 1930s Lost Heaven who gets dragged into the Salieri crime family after being in the wrong place at the wrong time.

From there, things go downhill pretty quickly.

What starts as Tommy doing a few jobs for the family slowly turns into shootouts, car chases, robberies and a lot of people making very bad decisions.

The story is easily the best part of the game.

It actually feels like a proper gangster film. The characters are memorable, the cutscenes are great and Tommy is genuinely interesting because he doesn't start off as some unstoppable criminal.

He's just a normal bloke who gets pulled further and further into that life.

Paulie and Sam are great as well, and by the end of the game you actually care about what happens to everyone.

The city itself looks brilliant too.

Lost Heaven absolutely nails the 1930s atmosphere. The old cars, streets, buildings, music and clothing all make the game feel like it belongs in that time period.

Driving around at night in the rain with some old music playing is honestly a vibe.

The gameplay is pretty simple.

You drive somewhere.

Shoot some people.

Drive somewhere else.

Probably shoot some more people.

And somehow it never really gets boring.

The shooting isn't anything revolutionary, but it feels decent enough and the missions usually keep things moving.

The driving is also a big part of the game, although some of the older cars handle like they've got shopping trolley wheels attached to them.

Obviously, it's not perfect.

The biggest problem is probably the open world.

Lost Heaven looks like a massive city that you should be able to explore for hours, but there really isn't that m…

Mafia: Definitive Edition is a benchmark for ground-up remakes and a glowing showcase of why the Mafia series remains my absolute favourite crime franchise in gaming. Rather than chasing generic open-world padding, it delivers a hyper-focused, cinematic mob masterpiece.

PROS

Unmatched Storytelling: Outstanding voice acting, motion capture, and dynamic character writing that feel straight out of a classic mob film.
Incredible 1930s Atmosphere: Lost Heaven is rendered in stunning detail, packed with interwar architecture, vintage vehicles, and an authentic period jazz soundtrack.
Satisfying Gunplay & Driving: Firearms carry genuine weight, and driving period automobiles requires actual skill, especially on classic settings.
Classic Mode Option: Features optional simulation-style driving physics, strict police responses for minor infractions, and realistic ammo loss on partial reloads.

CONS

Strict Linearity: The open world serves as a cinematic backdrop rather than an interactive sandbox, which may surprise players expecting a free-roam playground.
Melee Combat: Hand-to-hand brawling feels simple compared to the firearm mechanics.

VERDICT

If you love mature narrative-driven games, gripping period pieces, or classic mob stories, this is an absolute must-buy. Hangar 13 modernized a classic while preserving every ounce of its soul and emotional weight.

Final Score: 9.5/10 - Don Salieri sends his regards.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the racing mission on the highest difficulty setting is extremely frustrating and difficult.

citations.review_text:
Having never played the 2002 original, I came into this remake with fresh eyes, and I genuinely think it sets a high bar for how classic games should be remade. Everything feels carefully crafted—from the streets of Lost Heaven and its architecture to the period-appropriate cars and the people going about their daily lives. The story is straightforward and easy to follow, but it's elevated by memorable characters and offers an engaging glimpse into the lives of mobsters during the 1930s.

I played the game on Classic difficulty, and while I encountered a few bugs here and there, they never seriously detracted from the experience. The campaign never overstayed its welcome or became repetitive. It knew the story it wanted to tell and delivered it without unnecessary filler.

Except for that racing mission.

It's every bit as infamous as people say. I eventually had to cheat, and modify the games files a bit just to move on. Thankfully, that single frustrating chapter doesn't define the rest of the experience.

Ironically, despite the racing mission, I actually enjoyed the driving. The Classic driving model gives the cars a satisfying sense of weight, making every trip across Lost Heaven feel authentic. Considering how much time you'll spend behind the wheel, that's a very good thing. Gunplay is equally solid. The cover system is responsive and reliable, even if it doesn't do anything particularly groundbreaking.

The open world itself isn't meant to compete with the most dynamic sandbox games. It's primarily a backdrop for the story rather than a playground full of activities, and I know that may disappoint some players. Personally, I didn't mind. Lost Heaven excels as a place to soak in the atmosphere, cruise through its streets, and stop every now and then to admire the scenery or take screenshots. The city invites your imagination to fill in the gaps. If you look too closely, you'll notice that the illusion starts to crack, but as a stage for the narrative, it work…

9/10
Beautiful game, strong story, and exciting gameplay. I loved every minute of it except... THE CAR RACE. Dear god.... this level made me want to yeet my controller into a black hole. Whoever designed this "race" was on drugs, and not the good kind. They wanted to make you suffer and they do. It is completely broken and unfair. Legit almost made me not finish the game, but if you push through you are rewarded with some incredible scenes with maybe a couple familiar faces if you have played the other games.

great remake of a classic gem. the race mission is still a pain in the ass though! highly recommend watching a youtube video if stuck. besides that tho, do yourself the favor and play this enjoyable game

Mafia is a game close to my heart. When I heard that a remake of this legendary and groundbreaking game was in the works, I couldn’t pass it up.

The graphics are nice, and I’ve completed the game on the hardest difficulty, “Classic.” Paradoxically, it’s not that difficult to complete, but if there’s one part where you’ll definitely “hit a wall,” it’s the racing mission, which is a real test of patience on the hardest difficulty (I’m glad they stayed true to the original in this regard, where the race was also quite a challenge). In general, the driving in this game can be nerve-wracking, but you’ll get used to it over time! :D

The story is phenomenal and is guaranteed to draw you into this fictional world. After finishing the story, you’re free to roam the world at your leisure and use that time, for example, to collect all the collectibles if you’re the type of player who goes for achievements.

10/10!

Fantastic game with a great atmosphere, strong story, and memorable characters that make Lost Heaven feel alive from the start. The visuals are excellent, the driving and shooting feel good, and the whole game has a classy old school gangster charm. The only thing worth mentioning is the race mission on Classic difficulty, which feels less like a normal level and more like a cheerful little exercise in gamer masochism, but surviving it  makes the victory even sweeter. I definitely recommend this game.

Status: 100% Achievements / Platinum

Verdict: Average (Buy on sale only)

Pros
Lost Heaven and the car models look stunning. Smooth performance overall (aside from occasional slow texture rendering). Fantastic return of original voice actors (Tommy, Paulie). Reworked missions feel fresh and modern.

Cons
Story & dialogue alterations, worse than the 2002 original. Removing Tommy's framing narration in cutscenes takes away a lot of charm. Frank looks wrong; Salieri looks too young and uninteresting. Freeride mode beautiful world with nothing to do except a few annoying races. Awful collectible design, 195 collectibles is tedious bloat. Worse yet, several are locked inside story-mode interiors and can't be picked up in Free Ride. Motorcycle handling feels atrocious.
 
Not worth full price. The core story holds up, but narrative downgrades, an empty open world, and obnoxious collectible design hold it back. Grab it on a steep discount or in a bundle.

Hangar 13 did a very good job with the remake of this game although the story and graphics were very good i only hated the hardest difficulty of this game. i like a little challenge but it was very hard in my opinion also lets not forget the race in chapter 5 named " fair play ".

I enjoyed the story, graphics, driving mechanics, and atmosphere.

If you enjoy the mobster genre then this game is absolutely perfect for it. The characters are likeable and the plot is interesting and unique throughout. Almost all the missions are unique and bring something special to the table rather than being repetitive. Its important to note that the game is primarily driven through its story and the free play mode is more of an afterthought which can be seen with the side quests or various small activities in the city. So imagine GTA if it focused more on the story rather than the open world.

For me, the best seller was the story. A movie in video game form. The dialogue and acting is fantastic and if you love a story game with some combat and driving, then this is a great game to pick up.

There were moments in the game when the map was raining and dark and you were in a 1930s car, driving around the town with the radio on and it just hit a spot for me.
